Subject: Redline: Order Form + MSA — regulatory fines and third-party claims

Team — attaching our redline to the Order Form and a short note on two points that are blockers for procurement sign-off: statutory fines (GDPR/CCPA/PCI) and third-party claims tied to payment processing.

1) Statutory/regulatory fines: Acme needs an explicit carve-out from the liability cap for fines/penalties imposed by regulators that are directly related to processing of Acme customer data (GDPR/CCPA/PCI). We flagged this in the MSA redline as "statutory fines excluded from Limitation of Liability cap."

2) Third-party claims: if a card brand or payment processor issues a claim or fine related to Redwood's handling or configuration of the integration, we expect Redwood to indemnify Acme for those costs (including claimed penalties and reasonable defence costs).

We also included inline notes in the attached doc to clarify the scope (only fines directly caused by Redwood's breach of security obligations or willful misconduct). Procurement is asking for confirmation this language is acceptable, or a proposed counter that they can review quickly.

Marissa / Rishi — looping you in. Acme sent the attached redline and is asking for an explicit carve-out: statutory fines (GDPR/CCPA/PCI) excluded from LoL cap + indemnity for third-party processor claims when caused by us. Procurement wants a quick yes/no or an alternative redline.

My read: we should avoid an unconditional unlimited carve-out. Two quick options we can push back with:
- Option A (narrow carve-out): "To the extent required by applicable law, statutory fines and penalties imposed by a regulator will not be subject to the Liability Cap, provided such fines are directly attributable to Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct and Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to contest such fines where permitted."
- Option B (financial cap + insurance): keep regulatory fines within a higher, explicit cap (e.g., greater of $5M or 5x annual fees) and commit to maintain appropriate insurance; indemnity for third-party processor claims narrowly limited to claims arising from Redwood's breach of security obligations and subject to the same cap.

Rishi — can you draft language we can send back today? Procurement is on a tight timeline (they sign off this week if we land something acceptable). Ben / Marissa — if we've got any commercial flexibility on a numeric cap, call it out (I suspect Acme will push for unlimited).

Soojin / team / Acme — see proposed counter below. Kept it narrow and practical given Acme's ask and the regulatory exposure. Posting redline text inline for speed; I'll also attach a clean PDF with tracked changes.

--- Proposed counter (inline redline language for MSA "Limitation of Liability" section) ---
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, each party's liability for (a) death or bodily injury resulting from its negligence or willful misconduct, and (b) fines and penalties imposed by a governmental authority ("Regulatory Fines") shall be subject to the following: (i) to the extent a law requires that Regulatory Fines are not capable of being limited, such fines shall not be subject to the limitations set forth in this Section; (ii) otherwise, Redwood's aggregate liability for Regulatory Fines shall be limited to the greater of (A) $5,000,000 USD or (B) five (5) times the annual Subscription Fees paid under the applicable Order Form; provided, however, that Redwood shall only be liable for Regulatory Fines to the extent such fines directly result from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct in the performance of its obligations under the Agreement."

Indemnity (third-party claims): Redwood shall indemnify and hold Customer harmless from and against third-party claims to the extent such claims arise out of Redwood's breach of its obligations under the Agreement, including proven failure to maintain appropriate security controls for payment data or misconfiguration of the payment integration; provided that Redwood's indemnity obligations shall be subject to the same monetary limit set forth above for Regulatory Fines, and Customer shall reasonably cooperate with Redwood in the defence, and Redwood shall have the right to control the defence and settlement of any such claim.

Additional practical points:
- Require Customer to provide regulatory notice and full cooperation; Redwood retains the right to attempt to mitigate/contest fines.
- For PCI: require Acme to keep its environment and tokenization config per our integration guide; any failure on their side should carve back liability.
- We should offer to provide PCI attestation and SOC 2 report as a condition for accepting a higher cap.

I'm happy to send this back as a tracked redline PDF. If Acme refuses all caps and insists on unlimited exposure, we should escalate to Revenue Ops / CRO for approval.

Attachment: Redwood_Counter_Liability_20260223.pdf (pdf)

Soojin / Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. Procurement reviewed Rishi's counter. A few notes from Acme's side:

- The carve-out "to the extent required by applicable law" is fine, but we need a carve-out for fines that are not "required by law" where regulators typically impose penalties (e.g., GDPR breach fines tied to a data processing error). Our preference is for Regulatory Fines to be excluded from any cap when they relate to personal data obligations; however we understand Redwood's position on limiting exposure for willful misconduct.

- The dollar cap alternative is safer for both sides. If Redwood takes the $5M / 5x annual fees cap, Acme will require evidence of insurance (CYBER policy) and a SOC 2 Type II report. Can Redwood provide SOC2 + a PCI attestation within 3 business days?

- For third-party processor claims, Acme wants the indemnity to cover claims from card brands or acquirers to the extent Redwood's misconfiguration is the proximate cause. We accept the cooperation and defence control language but would like an express carve-out that allows Acme to pursue interim remediation payments and seek recovery later if necessary.

If you can confirm SOC2/PCI docs and accept the $5M / 5x cap (or increase to $10M for GDPR-specific fines), we can push this across procurement this week. Otherwise procurement will need to rerun a formal risk review which will delay signature.

Thanks —
Eve Martinez
Payments Program Manager, Acme Payments
